# Isolated staging and safe releases

**Live site:** https://archiveresp.dpdns.org/ — Cloudflare production Worker, GitHub `main`.

**Development:** GitHub `develop` — Cloudflare branch Preview, separate staging Supabase project. Its URL is generated by Cloudflare; do not guess it.

**Critical:** Although the existing Supabase project is named `canned-response-archive-dev`, that is the project used by the **live site** today. Treat it as production data until a separate migration is planned. Do not reuse its database key, sessions, avatars, PIN pepper, or private response exports for staging.

## Branch strategy

| Branch | Use | Deployment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main` | Approved releases only | Production Worker and existing domain |
| `develop` | Redesign integration and testing | Separate Cloudflare Preview |
| `feature/<description>` | Individual changes branched from `develop` | Pull-request Preview if enabled |

Create feature branches from `develop`. Merge them into `develop` after review. When the whole redesign passes tests and visual checks, open a **release pull request targeting `main`**. Merging it is the explicit production release.

GitHub Actions verify and security-audit workflows run on both `main` and `develop` pushes and on pull requests. The cleanup workflow intentionally exempts both long-lived branches.

### Protect branches in GitHub

Under **GitHub → Repository Settings → Rules → Rulesets** (or Branch protection), require pull requests and passing verify/security checks before changes to `main`, and ideally `develop`. Disable force pushes and deletion for both. Keep `main` as the repository default branch.

**GitHub currently reports `main` as unprotected.** These administrative rules are not applied by merely creating `develop` and must be configured and verified separately.

## Set up the Cloudflare Preview

The existing `wrangler.jsonc` already has `"previews": {}` and supports modern Worker Previews.

1. Open **Cloudflare → Workers & Pages → canned-response-archive → Settings → Builds → Branch control**.
2. **Keep Production branch set to `main`**. Do not alter its Worker name, custom domain, routes or secrets.
3. Enable **Preview Builds**. If Cloudflare offers **Set up Worker Previews** for an existing Worker, review the one-time switch carefully; this is a Cloudflare dashboard setting.
4. Check the Worker's **Previews** section for the `develop` Preview URL after a push. It must be distinct from the production domain.
5. Until staging credentials are configured, the Preview can show the frontend but authenticated API calls return a missing-backend-configuration error.

Older version-preview URLs and older Builds integrations can behave differently. Verify the preview deployment's *actual* bindings before storing any test account data. Cloudflare Worker Previews keep Preview variables, secrets, and code separate from production by default.

Cloudflare Preview URLs are public by default. Keep testing data synthetic, and use **Cloudflare Access** before sharing staging if it contains private test material.

Official documentation:
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/ci-cd/builds/build-branches/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/previews/get-started/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/previews/configuration/

## Provision a separate Supabase project

Create a brand-new Supabase project named something like `canned-response-archive-staging`. Check your Supabase plan's available project quota and any associated cost before creating it. Apply all SQL files in `supabase/migrations/` **to that new project only**, in chronological order. Use fresh test accounts; an empty installation's first completed signup claims administrator.

Never copy live customer replies, accounts, PIN hashes, sessions, rate limits, or OTP records into staging. Any sample responses should be fictitious.

Supply the following values to the **`develop` Preview**, not Production:
- `SUPABASE_URL`: the new staging project's URL
- `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`: its server-side key, entered as a secret
- `PIN_PEPPER`: an independent, freshly generated 32+-character secret
- `OTP_MAILER_URL` and `OTP_MAILER_SECRET`: optional, for approved staging email tests
- `TMDB_READ_ACCESS_TOKEN`: optional

Cloudflare dashboard: **Worker → Settings → Variables and Secrets → Previews Base** is available for preview secrets shared by new Previews. Prefer setting the three mandatory secrets only on the persistent `develop` Preview if other feature branches should not inherit access to the same staging database. A local Wrangler command can set one Preview's secret:

```bash
npx wrangler preview secret put SUPABASE_URL --name develop
npx wrangler preview secret put SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY --name develop
npx wrangler preview secret put PIN_PEPPER --name develop
```

Each command prompts for its value. Do not enter real keys into chat, GitHub, code files or public screenshots. Existing Previews do not automatically inherit later changes to Previews Base secrets. Never use real production secrets in Previews Base.

For local Vite work, use the gitignored `.dev.vars` file pointing to the new staging project. Do not edit the committed `.dev.vars.example` to contain actual keys.

## Before merging back into `main`

1. `npm ci && npm run check`, and require the GitHub Actions checks to succeed.
2. Test the Preview in dark/light mode, small/mobile layouts, keyboard navigation, 200% zoom, reduced-motion preference, and lower-end devices.
3. Exercise the Worker API against **test** accounts: guest Shared access, private owner-only data, email/name login, import/export, moving visibility, By me filtering and bulk deletion.
4. Review all changes and any migrations independently. Database schema changes can affect live records even when the UI build succeeds.
5. Prepare a rollback plan; back up live data for schema-changing releases and record the previous known-good Cloudflare deployment.
6. Open `develop` → `main` PR, review the final diff, merge after approval, and verify the **new production** Cloudflare build and live behavior.

Reverting code or restoring an earlier Cloudflare Worker version **does not roll back Supabase migrations or recover deleted records**. Treat database migrations as separate, deliberate operations.
